topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Hallmarks and Lecture Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the learning outcomes and establishes the framework of cancer hallmarks and multistep tumor progression for the lecture.

topics.label: Deregulated Growth and Survival Signaling Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in cell-surface receptors and intracellular cascades drive independent proliferation and resistance to growth-inhibitory signals.

topics.label: Differentiation Block in Tumor Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how impaired terminal differentiation allows cells to remain proliferative across hematopoietic malignancies and epithelial carcinomas.

topics.label: Evasion of Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how cancer cells resist programmed cell death through mutations disrupting p53, Bax, and BCL2 signaling.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality and Senescence Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells achieve infinite replicative potential by overcoming telomere shortening, senescence barriers, and p53-dependent stress responses.

topics.label: Metabolic Rewiring in Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how cancer cells alter their metabolic pathways to support rapid growth and reprogram the epigenome.

topics.label: Induction of Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how tumors stimulate new blood vessel growth to overcome hypoxia and sustain progression.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Patterns of Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the multistage metastatic cascade, circulatory dissemination, and genomic factors enabling secondary tumor formation.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Hallmark Synthesis
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer summarises the core takeaways on cancer hallmarks and concludes the session with practical logistics.
